findings.text: Migration assigns ownerless legacy data to the next account. Node VM repro on 1a713b8: upgrade tab A, then run 42aed7c's saveWikiDraft in an unreloaded A tab; B calls claimLocalData(2). B.loadWikiDraft('home').body returns A_SYNTHETIC_WIKI_DRAFT. Removing fallback ownership in memory returns null. Quarantine unattributed legacy data instead of assigning it to whoever signs in next.

Sign-out can delete another account's newly persisted unsent message. Node VM repro: shared unsent list contains a1,b1; pause A.clearLocalAccountData(1) after getItem, let B persist b2, then resume A's setItem. Output: [b1], expected [b1,b2]. An in-memory actor-scoped prefix mutation preserves both. Use actor-scoped keys or transactional updates so A's cleanup cannot overwrite B's writes.

The new asynchronous slug lookup can override a later navigation. Node VM ran actual applyRoute/conversationBySlug: hold the lookup for #fresh, navigate to known #general, then release fresh. Output: opened=[5,7], activeId=7, lastRequestedSlug=general. A route guard added in memory yields opened=[5], activeId=5. Recheck navigation identity and session generation after the lookup before opening a conversation or rendering no-access.
